title: Autonomous Drayage Dispatch: Guarding Agents Against Real-World Events

scenes.narration: Terminal gates retry webhooks and deliver them out of order. Turn every event into an LLM tool call and you double-book chassis, send trucks to boxes that already left, and miss demurrage.

Make it a state machine instead. Ingest and acknowledge fast. Evaluate in fixed order: dedupe the event id, drop anything older than what you know, check dwell. Only then take a Redis SET NX lock on the chassis and call the carrier.

The guard is plain typed Python. Events carry terminal time, not arrival time. Past seventy-two hours of dwell, with a twenty-four hour buffer before free time ends, the guard reserves the chassis exactly once.

Seven events: a retry, a second feed for the same box, an outgate that beats its own availability. Two dispatches, zero double reservations, one stale event dropped, all asserted, plus a throughput benchmark held above fifty thousand events per second.
Let the model reason, but let code own the side effects. Full source is in the companion repo: github.com/RichKingsASU/agentsinstitute.
